summary.headline: Ajanta Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25% to Rs 1,626 crore and PAT 31% to Rs 334 crore, with Asia branded generics down 16% on Middle East supply disruption.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 25% YoY to Rs 1,626 crore and PAT grew 31% to Rs 334 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up 21% to Rs 454 crore (28% margin). Growth was led by the US generics (+57%), Africa branded (+30%) and India (+24%), while Asia branded generics fell 16% to Rs 255 crore because Middle East geopolitical disruption delayed dispatches. Management said some Asia sales slipped into Q2 and kept full-year guidance of high-teens growth for Asia, while cutting US generics guidance back to mid-single digit for the rest of the year. An interim dividend of Rs 32 per share (about Rs 400 crore) was declared.

segments.name: Asia branded generics
segments.commentary: Sales Rs 255 crore vs Rs 304 crore, down 16% YoY, as Middle East supply chain disruption hit dispatches. Three new products launched; management says some sales slipped into Q2.

segments.name: Africa branded generics
segments.commentary: Sales Rs 295 crore vs Rs 228 crore, up 30% YoY; 34% of group revenue combined with Asia. Three new products launched in the quarter.

segments.name: US generics
segments.commentary: Sales Rs 487 crore vs Rs 310 crore, up 57% YoY, 30% of revenue, supported by two launches. Full-year guidance cut to mid-single-digit growth, with price erosion and share loss expected later.

segments.name: Africa institutional business
segments.commentary: Sales Rs 70 crore vs Rs 38 crore, up 83% YoY, c.4% of revenue.

segments.name: India branded business
segments.commentary: Sales Rs 509 crore vs Rs 409 crore, up 24% YoY, 32% of revenue, with eight launches. Trade generics Rs 48 crore vs Rs 39 crore. IQVIA MAT June data shows growth of 15% vs IPM 11%.

guidance_outlook: Overall: growth momentum of high teens for FY27 (management stated at start of call).
Gross margin for full year around 78%, plus or minus 100 bps (Q1 actual 80%).
Adjusted EBITDA margin around 27% for full year, plus or minus 100 bps, excluding forex.
R&D expenditure around 5% of revenue for full year (Q1 about 4%).
Effective tax rate around 26% for full year.
Capex of about Rs 400 crore for FY27, of which about Rs 100 crore maintenance and about Rs 300 crore for the Pithampur emerging-markets expansion.
US generics: mid-single-digit growth for FY27 (upper end slightly above); no launches in Q2 or Q3, with more launches hoped for in Q4 subject to FDA approvals; 5 to 7 filings expected in FY27.
Asia branded generics: high-teens growth guidance for FY27 maintained; Q2 expected to be elevated by carry-forward of sales.
Africa branded generics: high double-digit growth for FY27, with the run rate expected to be a little lower than Q1's 30%.
Africa institutional: high double-digit growth for FY27.
India: mid-teens growth guidance for FY27 maintained.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex Rs 83 crore; FY27 capex planned at about Rs 400 crore.
About Rs 300 crore of FY27 capex is for expansion at the Pithampur plant, for emerging markets.
Around 50 international MRs added in Q1.

India MR productivity (PCPM) at Rs 4.5 lakh in Q1 per management; ophthalmology productivity said to be at par or better than top peers, while gynaecology and nephrology are below industry average as they are under 18 months old.
New geographies (Asia, Middle East, Latin America) expected to play out in 3 to 5 years.
demand_pricing: India: volume growth 4.7% vs IPM volume growth 3.4%; new launches and volume drove growth, with price in line with IPM. Cardiology 37%, ophthalmology 29%, dermatology 22%, pain 10%, new therapies 2% of India branded sales.
Africa: market growing 7% to 12% YoY; Ajanta growing well ahead of the market.

US: growth is carry-forward momentum from prior quarters; management expects competition, price erosion and share loss in coming quarters. Most of the US business comes from existing products; the two Q1 launches have not yet contributed meaningfully.

Asia: management says demand is not constrained; the constraint is logistics and supply chain. Raw material cost inflation is being discussed, but inventory held meant little Q1 impact, with possible impact from Q2.
Semaglutide India: market has plateaued; MAT market size around Rs 850 crore in 12 months per management. Asia and Africa launches are about 2 years away.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the IQVIA India growth (15%) inconsistent with reported India growth (24%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IQVIA figures are MAT-based; on a three-month basis the market grew about 18% vs Ajanta's 24%. Differences between IPM and internal numbers are normal.

qa_highlights.question: How much Asia sales will be pushed into Q2 and how confident is the recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not quantify the carry-forward but said Q2 will be elevated; supplies have been made and sales will be realised once stock reaches destination. Management is reasonably confident, and full-year Asia guidance is high-teens growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was US growth 57% and what is the outlook for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Momentum carried forward from prior quarters. Full-year guidance is mid-single digit, with competition, price erosion and share loss factored in for coming quarters. Next year's guidance not given.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin guidance of 78% vs 80% Q1: any input cost headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said mix and US price erosion drive the expected decline; raw material inflation is not yet affecting numbers due to inventory, but may start from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Personnel cost rose from Rs 341 crore in Q4 to Rs 381 crore in Q1 (about 12%), mainly from increments plus about 50 added international MRs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 27% EBITDA guidance inclusive of forex loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance excludes forex, which is volatile; Q1 had a Rs 20 crore net forex gain recorded across other income and other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Action plan to match IPM growth in cardiology, and how does PCPM compare with peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says internal growth matches or beats cardiac segment growth and the gap is IQVIA data capture, which is being corrected with the agency. PCPM is Rs 4.5 lakh in Q1; peers are not directly comparable due to segment mix, with ophthalmology productivity at par or better and gynaecology and nephrology below average.

risks_watch: Middle East and geopolitical disruption to Asia logistics; Q2 recovery depends on delayed shipments being realised.
US generics: competition, price erosion and share loss expected to slow growth towards mid-single digit; US tariff policy uncertainty (Section 232 generics, possible review around August 2028).
Raw material cost inflation from geopolitical issues may hit gross margin from Q2.
US launch pipeline has no launches in Q2 and Q3; Q4 depends on FDA approvals.
Cardiology IQVIA data capture gap in India, and India semaglutide market plateauing at about Rs 850 crore.
Opex growth of 32% YoY and a Rs 31 crore forex loss in Q1; Africa growth expected to moderate from 30%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India, Africa and overall momentum, but cautious and somewhat evasive on Asia timing and US normalisation. Management repeatedly deferred quantification (Asia carry-forward, next-year US guidance, operating cash flow) and blamed external factors for Asia and the US outlook.
key_quotes: Asia, unfortunately, the current quarter again, the disruption which has happened because of the geopolitical issues, which started again.
So with that getting streamlined, we should be able to get the stocks into the market and then that should continue.
It is excluding the forex because forex loss is something which is very uncertain.
Normally, we give out the guidance of the current year only.

growth.why: Management reiterates high-teens overall FY27 growth, with India mid-teens, Africa high double-digit and Asia high-teens, backed by launches, MR additions and volume gains, but US guidance was cut to mid-single digit and no specific orders or capacity timing were given for the growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin guided to around 78% +/-100 bps for FY27 vs Q1 actual 80%, and adjusted EBITDA margin guided to around 27% vs Q1 28%, as US price erosion, mix and raw material inflation from Q2 weigh.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About Rs 300 crore of the Rs 400 crore FY27 capex is for Pithampur emerging-markets expansion, with Q1 capex at Rs 83 crore, but no commissioning date was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: India volume grew 4.7% vs IPM 3.4%, Africa branded +30% in Q1, and Asia Q2 is guided to be elevated by carry-forward, though US growth slows to mid-single digit.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of about Rs 400 crore is already planned for FY27 and Pithampur is under way, but utilisation was not disclosed, so no new capex round is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: US generics guidance was cut to mid-single digit and the rest of the guidance was held, with no sign of a raise; Asia upside depends on carry-forward being realised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: US generics was already cut to mid-single digit from high-teens-type expectations, with price erosion and share loss expected, and Asia depends on Middle East shipments that have slipped.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No US launches in Q2 or Q3, with Q4 launches hoped for subject to FDA approvals; 5 to 7 US filings expected in FY27, and India had eight launches in Q1.

rows.label: Asia and Middle East / LatAm expansion
rows.why: Management expects new geographies to play out over 3 to 5 years, with about 50 international MRs added in Q1, but Asia is currently constrained by logistics.

rows.label: Asia carry-forward sales into Q2
rows.why: Supplies have been made and Q2 is expected to be elevated by carry-forward from Q1's Rs 255 crore Asia sales (down 16% YoY), though the amount was not quantified.

rows.label: US price erosion and share loss
rows.why: Management expects competition, price erosion and share loss in coming quarters, which is why US generics was cut to mid-single digit after 57% growth in Q1.
